item.title: China's longest metro loop line enters full operation in Wuhan
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
A train runs on the Wuhan Metro Line 12 in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Oct. 29, 2026. China's longest subway loop line, the Wuhan Metro Line 12, started full line operation on Thursday. The 59.9-km line has 37 stations and stretches across seven administrative districts of the city. By far, the total mileage of Wuhan Metro in operation has exceeded 581 kilometers. (Xinhua/Xiao Yijiu) WUHAN, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- Metro Line 12 in Wuhan, the capital of central China's Hubei Province, became fully operational on Thursday, making it China's longest metro loop line, according to the China Association of Metros. Stretching 59.9 kilometers and serving 37 underground stations across seven urban districts of Wuhan, the line connects the Wuchang and Hankou railway hubs and offers transfers to 18 existing and planned lines. A full loop takes about 96 minutes. The line opened in two phases. The first phase, 35.3 kilometers long, entered service on May 1 this year. With the second phase now operational, Wuhan Metro's operational length exceeds 581 kilometers, roughly the driving distance between Berlin and Munich or between Rome and Milan. Wuhan, known as the "river city," has complex geological and hydrological conditions, which posed multiple challenges during construction. The line passes under the Yangtze River twice and the Hanjiang River once. Construction teams overcame a series of technical difficulties, including high water pressure and composite strata. One cross-river tunnel, in particular, is approximately 4 kilometers long, with its lowest point 71.4 meters below the Yangtze River surface. The project has provided valuable experience for building super-large-diameter cross-river tunnels in China. Wuhan, home to over 13.86 million permanent residents, is a key transport hub in China and a core city of the Yangtze River Economic Belt. The opening of Metro Line 12 is expected to further facilitate cross-river commuting. China has issued a plan to comprehensively advance the high-quality development of integrated transport services during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the Ministry of Transport announced in July this year. The plan aims to basically establish a modern integrated transport service system by 2030. Under the plan, China will improve connections among different modes of transport, make passenger transfers more convenient and enhance freight logistics services. ■ People take an escalator at a station of the Wuhan Metro Line 12 in Wuhan, central China's Hubei Province, Oct. 29, 2026. item.title: Beyond protected areas, diverse stakeholders help conserve biodiversity in China
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
YEREVAN, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- Diverse conservation efforts in China are demonstrating how biodiversity can be safeguarded beyond designated protected areas through cooperation, with local communities, researchers, businesses and government agencies playing complementary roles, a Chinese conservationist has said at a United Nations biodiversity event. At a thematic event titled "Multi-Stakeholder Strategies and Actions for Biodiversity Conservation," held at the China Pavilion during the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17) in the Armenian capital of Yerevan, conservation efforts at China's Weitou Bay Wetland were highlighted as a successful example of such efforts. More than 1 percent of the estimated global population of critically endangered spoon-billed sandpipers has been recorded wintering at Weitou Bay Wetland in Quanzhou, southeast China's Fujian Province, in each of the past three winters, said Yan Baohua, secretary-general of China's Mangrove Conservation Foundation (MCF). The wetland is not a designated protected area. The spoon-billed sandpiper breeds in Russia's Far East and migrates thousands of kilometers along the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, relying on coastal stopovers and wintering habitats. Yet only about 15 percent of the predicted suitable intertidal habitats for the species lie within protected areas, according to a study cited by Yan. The MCF and Beijing Forestry University launched a spoon-billed sandpiper conservation project in 2018, Yan said, noting that surveys conducted across southern China from 2019 to 2026 identified additional wintering sites, many outside protected areas, highlighting the need to extend conservation efforts beyond the existing protected-area network. At Weitou Bay Wetland, conservation efforts had long been driven largely by local bird-watching volunteers. In March 2025, the MCF partnered with local bird-watching groups and government departments to establish a conservation station to better coordinate protection efforts. Bird-watching groups now conduct regular monitoring and patrols, while local prosecutors contribute to habitat protection through public-interest litigation. Villagers are also working to establish their own patrol teams. Another example of community involvement comes from Sanniang Bay in Qinzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, where fishermen in a community outside a nature reserve are helping protect horseshoe crabs accidentally caught in fishing nets. Song Xin of the Farmers' Seed Network said that when her team visited the area in 2019, adult horseshoe crabs caught in fishing nets were sold to local restaurants, while subadults were discarded because they had no commercial value. With support from the network, local residents established a rescue and release group in 2021 to return accidentally caught horseshoe crabs to the sea. Song said reports of fewer horseshoe crabs in local fishermen's nets prompted her team and scientists to survey the area. They found that Sanniang Bay hosts adult and subadult horseshoe crabs, while spawning grounds and juvenile habitats lie farther east near the Dafeng River estuary, underscoring the need to extend conservation efforts beyond the bay. Biodiversity conservation efforts are also extending into urban spaces. At Nanjing Hongshan Forest Zoo in east China's Jiangsu Province, nearly 700 species of native wildlife, including around 130 bird species, have been recorded, according to Wei Ye, director of sustainability at the zoo. An artificial lake once lined with hardened banks has undergone ecological restoration, creating more natural shorelines and improving the connection between the water and shoreline vegetation. Wei said Chinese water deer had given birth near the restored lake at the zoo this year. The examples illustrate China's efforts to explore other effective area-based conservation measures (OECMs), which complement protected areas. Recognized under Target 3 of the 2022 Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the OECMs contribute to the goal of effectively conserving at least 30 percent of the world's land, inland waters, coastal and marine areas by 2030. Madhu Rao, chair of the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) World Commission on Protected Areas, said the target could not be achieved through protected areas alone. "One of the big advantages of OECMs is that they allow us to recognize the stewardship of nature by non-state actors, as it's so well established in the example from China," she said. The thematic event was organized by the All-China Environment Federation and the China Environmental Protection Foundation. ■

item.title: China to take all necessary measures should EU impose discriminatory trade restrictions: commerce ministry
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- China will take all necessary measures to safeguard its interests and the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese enterprises if the European Union (EU) insists on imposing discriminatory restrictions on Chinese products, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday. Ministry spokesperson Huang Ling made the remarks at a regular news conference in response to media reports that the EU is considering extending the understanding reached between China and the EU on hybrid vehicle trade to other sectors such as chemicals. Imposing artificial barriers to normal trade may violate World Trade Organization rules and would not help improve the competitiveness of EU industries. Instead, such measures would place a heavier burden on downstream industries, pushing up inflation in the EU and undermining the security and stability of global industrial and supply chains, Huang said. Huang said the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism, held recently, made positive progress and yielded a number of agreed outcomes, showing that both sides have the willingness, ability and wisdom to properly manage their economic and trade differences through dialogue and consultation. China has repeatedly stressed that it is a partner in addressing the problems facing the EU, rather than the source of those problems, Huang said, adding that China is willing to strengthen dialogue and consultation with the EU, continue exploring solutions to each other's economic and trade concerns, and promote upward balancing and forward progress in China-EU trade. China firmly opposes any protectionist practices involving the abuse of trade defense instruments, Huang said. ■

item.title: China expands foreign business access at world's largest free trade port
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- China has unveiled 16 measures to make it easier for foreign businesses and professionals to operate in the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP), the world's largest FTP by area, with new policies covering energy trade, medical services and bonded business operations, according to a government circular made public Thursday. Under the measures, foreign physicians legally licensed to practice medicine overseas may obtain permits to provide clinical diagnosis and treatment services in Hainan for up to three years, with extensions available in accordance with relevant regulations. More convenient policies regarding work permits and stay and residence will also be introduced for foreign nationals. The Hainan FTP, located in China's southernmost island province, launched island-wide special customs operations in December 2025, allowing freer entry of overseas goods, expanded zero-tariff coverage and more business-friendly measures as part of China's efforts to promote high-standard opening-up. Overseas companies will be allowed to use bonded facilities at Hainan's liquefied natural gas (LNG) receiving terminals, while the FTP will be supported in conducting LNG futures delivery warehouse operations after LNG futures contracts are launched. Other measures include promoting offshore trade, expanding the range of products eligible for bonded maintenance, facilitating the entry of eligible bonded remanufactured products into pilot free trade zones on the Chinese mainland, encouraging the use of the yuan in new forms of barter trade, and deepening the FTP's economic and trade cooperation with China's Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. Bonded remanufactured products entering mainland pilot free trade zones will be subject to applicable import tariffs, import-related value-added tax and consumption tax. They must also meet all applicable technical requirements for equivalent new products and relevant regulations on remanufactured products, and be clearly labeled as such. The circular also calls for improved insurance products and services in areas such as international transportation and bonded maintenance. The latest measures come amid robust growth in Hainan's foreign trade. In the first three quarters of 2026, the province's goods imports and exports reached 285.44 billion yuan (about 42.5 billion U.S. dollars), up 49.8 percent year on year, while trade in services rose 11.7 percent to 56.95 billion yuan, according to data from Hainan's provincial commerce authorities. Trade in maintenance and repair services more than doubled year on year to 3.31 billion yuan during the same period, according to the provincial commerce department. The trade mainly came from imports of aircraft materials and components and revenues from aircraft maintenance services. The number of newly established foreign-invested enterprises in Hainan rose 38.6 percent year on year in the first half of 2026, according to the State Administration for Market Regulation. The FTP measures are part of China's broader efforts to promote high-standard opening-up. The country has announced plans to further expand pilot opening-up programs in sectors such as value-added telecommunications, biotechnology and wholly foreign-owned hospitals, while taking steps to facilitate cross-border trade and investment. The circular was jointly issued by the Ministry of Commerce, the National Development and Reform Commission, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the General Administration of Customs. ■

item.title: Xi extends condolences over deadly train collision in Spain
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday sent a message of condolence to Spanish King Felipe VI over the deadly high-speed train collision in the Spanish province of Toledo. In the message, Xi expressed deep condolences for the victims and sincere sympathies to the bereaved families on behalf of the Chinese government and people upon learning that the accident caused heavy casualties. He also wished those injured in the tragic crash a speedy recovery. Also on Thursday, Chinese Premier Li Qiang sent a message of condolence to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. ■

item.title: CPC plenum concludes, adopting resolution on persevering with full, rigorous Party self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-29
BEIJING, Oct. 29 (Xinhua) -- The 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) held its fifth plenary session from Monday to Thursday in Beijing, adopting a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. The Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee presided over the meeting. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, delivered an important address, said a communique issued after the session. At the session, participants heard and discussed a report on the work of the Political Bureau presented by Xi. They also considered and adopted the Resolution of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance. Xi delivered explanatory remarks on the draft of the resolution. The CPC Central Committee fully affirmed the work of the Political Bureau since the committee's fourth plenary session, the communique said. Looking back on the Party's journey since its founding, the CPC Central Committee pointed out that the key to the success of the CPC in winning one victory after another lies in its pursuit of the high ideal of communism, its dedication to achieving lasting greatness for the Chinese nation, and its commitment to seeking happiness for the Chinese people and rejuvenation for the Chinese nation. At the session, the CPC Central Committee gave a highly positive assessment of the great achievements the Party has made in exercising full and rigorous self-governance in the new era. It was pointed out that as the Party endeavors to supervise, govern, develop, and strengthen itself in the new era, the CPC Central Committee with Comrade Xi Jinping at its core has put forward a series of new ideas, new thinking, and new strategies in response to the major questions of the times -- what kind of long-term governing Marxist party the CPC should build and how to build it, thereby giving rise to Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. "It was stressed that many favorable conditions are now in place for advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, while we also face many new circumstances and new issues in this endeavor," the communique said. Profound changes in global, national, and Party conditions have made the CPC's tasks of uniting and leading the people in safeguarding China's sovereignty, security, and development interests, of uniting and leading the people in promoting reform and development and maintaining social harmony and stability, and of maintaining its advanced nature and integrity even more formidable, it added. "Dedicated to fulfilling the Party's missions and tasks, we must act in line with the overall requirements for Party building in the new era, take the Party Constitution as our fundamental guide, maintain the Party's vanguard nature, and uphold the overall leadership of the Party and the centralized, unified leadership of the Party Central Committee," the communique said. At the session, the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were highlighted as follows: serving the Party's missions and tasks; taking strengthening the Party politically as the overarching principle; exercising rigorous governance across the board; adopting a problem-oriented approach; upholding fundamental principles and breaking new ground; adhering to a top-down approach; and running the Party according to regulations. Systematic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance were also made at the session, according to the communique. Strengthening the Party spirit represents a fundamental task in the CPC's efforts to ensure full and rigorous Party self-governance, it said. Democratic centralism is the Party's fundamental organizational principle and leadership system, and its implementation is therefore an inherent requirement for exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, the communique added. Strict management of officials is the key to full and rigorous Party self-governance, it noted. "We will build up the ranks of high-caliber officials with firm political commitment, outstanding professional competence, excellent work conduct, and strict discipline," it added. Party organizations at all levels play the principal role in exercising full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique, adding that it is therefore essential to systematically advance the development of Party organizations at all levels and in all sectors to strengthen their political and organizational functions. Improving conduct and tightening discipline are effective measures to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. "It was noted that taking integrated steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity, or desire to commit corruption is both an important strategy for full and rigorous Party self-governance and a fundamental guideline for our fight against corruption," the communique said. "We must take systematic steps to address both symptoms and root causes of corruption and adopt a holistic approach that combines severe punishment, targeted remedy, and effective prevention, carrying this fight through to the end," it stated. Strengthening Party regulations and institutions represents a long-term, fundamental strategy for ensuring full and rigorous Party self-governance, said the communique. Persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance entails further improvement to Party and state oversight systems, said the communique, adding that it is the common political responsibility of all Party members. Studying and implementing the guiding principles from this plenary session represent a major political task for the entire Party both at present and in the period to come, according to the communique. It was also stressed that all aspects of the Party's work agenda should be steadily advanced at the turn of the year. The CPC Central Committee decided at the session that the Party will convene its 21st National Congress in Beijing in the second half of 2027 and stated that this congress, which is to be held at a critical stage for basically realizing socialist modernization and on a new journey toward the Second Centenary Goal, will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country. The session elected Zhang Shengmin as a new member of the CPC Central Committee Political Bureau, according to the communique. The session also decided on the filling of empty seats on the Central Committee by alternate members, deliberated and adopted inspection reports of the Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the Central Military Commission on those committing grave violations of discipline and laws, and confirmed the Political Bureau's previous decisions to punish those violators. The CPC Central Committee called upon the entire Party to rally more closely around the CPC Central Committee with Xi at its core and fully implement Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. ■

item.title: Why the CPC puts people's well-being at the heart of self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-27
BEIJING, Oct. 27 (Xinhua) -- In northeast China's Heilongjiang Province, eligible residents can receive certain forms of medical assistance and other support without submitting an application. Government departments share the information needed to provide the benefits. The provincial bodies responsible for disciplinary inspection helped drive the change. They prompted civil affairs departments to build a data-sharing network connecting 33 departments and institutions, enabling 12 frequently used assistance services to be provided without applications. The initiative offers a concrete example of how the self-supervision of the Communist Party of China (CPC) improve public services and help ensure that benefits reach those who most need them. Earning public trust through tangible improvements in people's lives is a defining feature of the CPC's full and rigorous self-governance, which is high on the agenda of the fifth plenary session of its 20th Central Committee. The key meeting, which opened Monday in Beijing, is considering a draft decision of the CPC Central Committee on major issues concerning strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance. COMMITMENT TO THE PEOPLE The CPC constitution commits the Party to serving the people, and states that it has no special interests of its own apart from those of the working class and the broadest possible majority of the people. Without seeking self-interest, the CPC can keep its spirit of thorough self-reform, and by swiftly detecting and resolving its own problems, the Party can prevent any interest group, power group or privileged stratum from preying on or corrupting its members. Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, has led an unprecedented anti-corruption campaign since 2012, driven by a determination to "offend a few thousand rather than fail 1.4 billion." The campaign has targeted corrupt officials at both high and low levels. Gyula Thurmer, president of the Hungarian Workers' Party, said serving the interests of the people is a central principle of the CPC. He added that the Party's anti-corruption efforts have achieved significant results, strengthening internal discipline and helping implement major economic and social development programs. SAFEGUARDING PEOPLE'S INTERESTS Xi has called on Party members to bear in mind that "benefiting the people is their greatest political achievement." An official review of work in 2025 reported that disciplinary and supervisory bodies nationwide investigated 967,000 cases of misconduct and corruption affecting people's daily lives, returning or helping recover about 77.6 billion yuan (11.5 billion U.S. dollars) in money and property to the public. Faruk Boric, president of the Association of Friendship between China and Bosnia and Herzegovina, said China's efforts to pursue corrupt officials at both senior and lower levels send "a clear message that no official is above the rules, regardless of their position." He said China's experience offers important lessons in linking clean governance with people's well-being. Protecting public funds, he added, helps direct more resources toward health care, education and other public services. BUILDING BETTER GOVERNANCE On several occasions, Xi has called for taking simultaneous, coordinated, and comprehensive steps to ensure that officials do not have the audacity, opportunity or desire to become corrupt. In his article on the Party's self-reform, Xi urged efforts to improve Party conduct, enforce discipline, and fight corruption, while integrating Party self-supervision with public oversight to deeply advance the Party's self-reform. Lyazid Benhami, a member of the Paris Association of French-Chinese Friendship, said rigorous Party self-governance can clarify officials' responsibilities, improve coordination and help sustain development programs. He highlighted China's emphasis on long-term planning, infrastructure, education and research, adding that the country has achieved a profound transformation regarding such priority areas and improved the well-being of its people. Those administrative strengths matter as China implements its 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). In January, Xi urged efforts to confine power to an institutional cage in a more well-conceived and effective manner, and press ahead with the anti-corruption fight with a clearer understanding and stronger resolve, thus providing a strong guarantee for achieving the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan period. Volker Tschapke, honorary president of Germany's Prussian Society, said the CPC's courage to "turn the blade inward" demonstrated a "moral strength that I truly admire." He stressed that rigorous Party self-governance ultimately serves the fundamental interests of the people. "I have seen with my own eyes what that has achieved: how villages have blossomed through targeted poverty alleviation, how rural areas have found new hope, how high-speed rail connects people and hearts," he said.■
